meta.project: Bilingual, Ontology-Aware, and Explainable ESG Intelligence System
meta.description: Comprehensive reference mapping of the 5-layer integrated research plan to the curated literature corpus, establishing causal traceability from technical contributions to empirical evidence.

research_questions: RQ1.1: How can Transformer-based architectures be optimized for bilingual ESG ABSA?
RQ1.3: How can regional calibration and ESG lexicons mitigate bias?

literature_references.title: Improving Zero-shot Cross-lingual Transfer between Closely Related Languages by injecting Character-level Noise
literature_references.relevance: Provides empirical evidence that character-level noise improves zero-shot transfer for related languages, directly supporting the cross-lingual transfer goals of C3 and RQ1.1.

literature_references.title: Morphosyntactic Tagging with Pre-trained Language Models for Arabic and its Dialects
literature_references.authors: Go Inoue, Salam Khalifa, Nizar Habash
literature_references.relevance: Validates that strategic fine-tuning using datasets from high-resource dialects is beneficial for low-resource dialectal calibration, supporting the regional calibration approach in RQ1.3.

contributions: C8: Large-scale ESG LLM benchmark (30+ models)
research_questions: RQ2.1: To what extent does few-shot learning improve ESG granularity?
RQ2.4: How can multi-LLM fusion reduce hallucination?
RQ2.2: How can long-context mechanisms enhance scalability?

literature_references.title: Cutting Down on Prompts and Parameters: Simple Few-Shot Learning with Language Models
literature_references.authors: Robert L. Logan, Ivana Balazevic, Eric Wallace, Fabio Petroni, Sameer Singh, Sebastian Riedel
literature_references.relevance: Demonstrates that few-shot learning with minimal parameter updates can outperform standard fine-tuning, providing a baseline for few-shot granularity improvements in RQ2.1.

literature_references.title: Learning to Robustly Aggregate Labeling Functions for Semi-supervised Data Programming
literature_references.authors: Ayush Maheshwari, KrishnaTeja Killamsetty, Ganesh Ramakrishnan, Rishabh Iyer, Marina Danilevsky, Lucian Popa
literature_references.relevance: Establishes a framework for reweighting noisy labeling functions, providing the algorithmic logic for the weakly supervised training in C16.

research_questions: RQ3.1: How can symbolic reasoning be integrated using ESG ontologies?
RQ3.2: How can transparent outputs be ensured via reasoning graphs?
RQ3.3: How can implicit ESG claims be identified?

literature_references.title: Fact-Tree Reasoning for N-ary Question Answering over Knowledge Graphs
literature_references.authors: Yao Zhang, Peiyao Li, Hongru Liang, Adam Jatowt, Zhenglu Yang
literature_references.relevance: Introduces a tree-structured reasoning unit that improves interpretability over linear chains, providing the structural logic for reasoning graphs in C7 and RQ3.2.

literature_references.title: XPrompt: Explaining Large Language Model's Generation via Joint Prompt Attribution
literature_references.authors: Yurui Chang, Bochuan Cao, Yujia Wang, Jinghui Chen, Lu Lin
literature_references.relevance: Provides a counterfactual framework for joint prompt attribution, which aligns with the XAI techniques required for ontology-aligned explainability in C15 and RQ3.1.

research_questions: RQ4.1: How can XAI improve stakeholder trust in ESG outputs?
RQ4.5: Can tone–outcome mismatch reliably indicate greenwashing?

literature_references.title: Training Dynamics for Text Summarization Models
literature_references.authors: Tanya Goyal, Jiacheng Xu, Junyi Jessy Li, Greg Durrett
literature_references.relevance: Analyzes the stages where factual errors and hallucinations occur during training, supporting the development of mismatch detection for greenwashing in C11 and RQ4.5.

literature_references.title: Efficient Safety Alignment of Large Language Models via Preference Re-ranking and Representation-based Reward Modeling
literature_references.authors: Qiyuan Deng, Xuefeng Bai, Kehai Chen, Yaowei Wang, Liqiang Nie, Min Zhang
literature_references.relevance: Explores safety alignment through representation-based rewards, establishing a link between model reliability and stakeholder trust as pursued in RQ4.1.

research_questions: RQ5.1: How can transparent and auditable outputs be ensured?
RQ5.2: How can reasoning quality and consistency be operationalized at scale?

literature_references.title: Know Your Mistakes: Towards Preventing Overreliance on Task-Oriented Conversational AI Through Accountability Modeling
literature_references.authors: Suvodip Dey, Y. Sun, Gökhan Tür, Dilek Hakkani-Tür
literature_references.relevance: Proposes an accountability model to track dialogue state tracking errors, directly supporting the auditable output requirements in RQ5.1.

literature_references.title: What Works and Doesn’t Work, A Deep Decoder for Neural Machine Translation
literature_references.authors: Zuchao Li, Yiran Wang, M. Utiyama, E. Sumita, Hai Zhao, Taro Watanabe
literature_references.relevance: Identifies causes of deep-decoder failure in transformers and proposes stability fixes, which is critical for the operational scalability and efficiency goals in RQ5.2.
